message.content:
You are exploring the Go codebase at /bench/repo (the "memos" project). Answer two aggregation questions with evidence. Ignore web/ frontend and proto/gen generated code where sensible.

Q1: Which single function or method DECLARED under /bench/repo/internal/ has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) from the Go codebase? Candidates to check: internal/util helpers (e.g. util.GenUUID, ValidateEmail...), internal/base, internal/profile, errors helpers, etc. Method: list exported functions in internal/*, then for the top candidates run greps like `grep -rn "util.GenUUID(" --include=*.go /bench/repo | grep -v _test | wc -l` (also count with tests, report both). Report the winner: symbol — declaration path:line — approximate number of callers (non-test and total), plus the runner-up counts so the ranking is credible.

Q2: The data layer is the store package (/bench/repo/store). Its persistent entity types include Memo, User, Attachment (or Resource), Inbox, Reaction, IdentityProvider, UserSetting, MemoRelation, etc. For each major entity struct type, count how many DISTINCT Go packages OUTSIDE the store layer (i.e., not under /bench/repo/store) reference the type (grep for "store.Memo\b", "store.User\b", "*store.User", etc., collect unique package directories). Rank the top two types with rough package counts. Be careful to distinguish store.Memo from store.MemoRelation etc (use word boundaries).

Report structured facts with citations (declaration path:line for each winner).

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
All data collected. Here is the structured report.

## Q1: Highest fan-in function declared under /bench/repo/internal/

**Winner: `util.GenUUID()` — declared at /bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:40**
- Non-test callers: **7** call sites (server/auth/token.go, server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go, auth_service_session.go x2, shortcut_service.go, sso_username.go, user_service_access_tokens.go)
- Total including tests: **28** call sites (19 in server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go, 1 in authz_test.go, 1 in server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go)

Runner-up ranking (non-test / total call sites, excluding web/ and proto/gen):

| Rank | Symbol | Declaration | Non-test | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `util.GenUUID` | internal/util/util.go:40 | 7 | 28 |
| 2 | `filter.DefaultEngine` | internal/filter/engine.go:111 | 7 | 7 |
| 3 | `filter.AppendConditions` | internal/filter/helpers.go:9 | 6 | 6 |
| 4 | `util.ConvertStringToInt32` | internal/util/util.go:14 | 5 | 5 |
| 5 | `filter.DefaultAttachmentEngine` (engine.go:119) and `version.IsVersionGreaterThan` (internal/version/version.go:33) | | 4 | 4 |

Notes: `filter.DefaultEngine` ties GenUUID at 7 non-test callers (1 in server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go + memo.go and memo_relation.go in each of the 3 store/db dialects), but GenUUID wins decisively on total (28 vs 7). Apparent high counts elsewhere are false positives: `scheduler.New(` (12) is almost entirely doc comments and the package's own tests (2 non-test hits, both in internal/scheduler/doc.go comments); `util.HasPrefixes`, `util.ValidateEmail`, `util.ReplaceString` have 0 external callers. `base.` hits are mostly the `base.UIDMatcher` regexp var (8), not a function.

## Q2: store entity types by distinct packages outside /bench/repo/store

Counting unique package directories under server/ (nothing outside server/ references these types; web/ and proto/gen excluded; store/db/* and store/test excluded as inside the store layer):

**#1: `store.User` — declared at /bench/repo/store/user.go:29 — 7 outside packages**
server/auth, server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/api/v1/test, server/router/fileserver, server/router/frontend, server/router/rss (6 excluding the test package)

**#2: `store.Memo` — declared at /bench/repo/store/memo.go:35 — 6 outside packages**
server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/api/v1/test, server/router/frontend, server/router/rss, server/runner/memopayload (5 excluding the test package)

Full ranking of the rest: store.Attachment 4 (attachment.go:16 — api/v1, api/v1/test, fileserver, rss); store.Inbox 3 (inbox.go:24); store.MemoRelation 3 (memo_relation.go:16 — word-boundary grep `store\.MemoRelation\b` kept it distinct from store.Memo); store.MemoShare 3 (memo_share.go:6); store.Reaction 2 (reaction.go:7); store.UserIdentity 2 (user_identity.go:8); store.IdentityProvider (idp.go:12), store.UserSetting (user_setting.go:13), and store.InstanceSetting (instance_setting.go:14) have 0 outside-store package references — they are only used inside store/ and its db drivers (the API layer works with proto types for those).

Note: this repo names the file-entity type `Attachment` (store/attachment.go:16); there is no `store.Resource` type.
